judgments.yea_description: Voted for H.R. 3372, the One Stop Shop Community Reentry Program Act, which funded community organizations that help people leaving prison find housing, jobs, and services. The House passed it 259-167.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against H.R. 3372, the One Stop Shop Community Reentry Program Act, which funded community organizations that help people leaving prison find housing, jobs, and services. The House passed it 259-167.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for H.R. 7946, the Veteran Service Recognition Act, which let Homeland Security grant green cards to noncitizen military veterans facing deportation and required review of veterans already removed. The House passed it 220-208.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against H.R. 7946, the Veteran Service Recognition Act, which let Homeland Security grant green cards to noncitizen military veterans facing deportation and required review of veterans already removed. The House passed it 220-208.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for sending H.R. 8404, the Respect for Marriage Act, to the President, agreeing to the Senate version that repealed the federal definition of marriage as between a man and a woman and required states to recognize valid same-sex and interracial marriages. The House passed it 258-169, and it became law.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against sending H.R. 8404, the Respect for Marriage Act, to the President, which repealed the federal definition of marriage as between a man and a woman and required states to recognize valid same-sex and interracial marriages. The House passed it 258-169, and it became law.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for S. 3905, which required federal purchasing rules to be rewritten to identify and limit conflicts between contractors' private interests and government work. The House passed it 219-205, and it became law.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against S. 3905, which required federal purchasing rules to be rewritten to identify and limit conflicts between contractors' private interests and government work. The House passed it 219-205, and it became law.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for S. 4003, the Law Enforcement De-Escalation Training Act, which funded real-life police training to calm tense situations, avoid force, and respond to people in a mental health crisis. The House passed it 264-162, and it became law.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against S. 4003, the Law Enforcement De-Escalation Training Act, which funded real-life police training to calm tense situations, avoid force, and respond to people in a mental health crisis. The House passed it 264-162, and it became law.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for H.R. 9640, which required audits of every sitting president's tax return and public release of the returns and findings. The House passed it 222-201.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against H.R. 9640, which required audits of every sitting president's tax return and public release of the returns and findings. The House passed it 222-201.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for H.J.Res. 88 to cancel the Education Department's SAVE plan, the student loan plan that lowered payments based on income. The House passed it 210-189.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against H.J.Res. 88 to cancel the Education Department's SAVE plan, the student loan plan that lowered payments based on income. The House passed it 210-189.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for H.R. 2931, the Save SBA from Sanctuary Cities Act, which required the federal small-business agency to move any office located in a sanctuary area out of that area within 60 days. The House passed it 211-199.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against H.R. 2931, the Save SBA from Sanctuary Cities Act, which required the federal small-business agency to move any office located in a sanctuary area out of that area within 60 days. The House passed it 211-199.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for H.J.Res. 104 to cancel the federal land agency plan for the Miles City field office in eastern Montana, reopening those federal lands to coal leasing. The House passed it 211-208.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against H.J.Res. 104 to cancel the federal land agency plan for the Miles City field office in eastern Montana, reopening those federal lands to coal leasing. The House passed it 211-208.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for S.J.Res. 49, which would end the April 2, 2025 emergency used to place a 10 percent tariff on most imports and higher tariffs on some trading partners. The Senate tied 49-49, so it did not become law.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against S.J.Res. 49, which would end the April 2, 2025 emergency used to place a 10 percent tariff on most imports and higher tariffs on some trading partners. The Senate tied 49-49, so it did not become law.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for sending H.J.Res. 131 to the President to cancel the federal land agency decision limiting the coastal plain oil and gas leasing program and open more of the Arctic National Wildlife Refuge to drilling. The Senate passed it 49-45.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against sending H.J.Res. 131 to the President to cancel the federal land agency decision limiting the coastal plain oil and gas leasing program and open more of the Arctic National Wildlife Refuge to drilling. The Senate passed it 49-45.
